name: Bile Acid Synthesis Defect with Cholestasis and Malabsorption
aliases: Inborn Errors of Bile Acid Synthesis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for bile acid synthesis defects

criteria.description: Presence of persistent cholestasis with conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
Detection of abnormal bile acid metabolites in plasma or urine by mass spectrometry
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in bile acid synthesis (e.g., HSD3B7, AKR1D1)
Clinical evidence of fat malabsorption including steatorrhea and fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies
Histological findings consistent with cholestatic liver disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent cholestasis, abnormal bile acid profile, and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to initiate bile acid replacement therapy and prevent progressive liver damage.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormal bile acid metabolites detected by mass spectrometry
searchTerms: unusual bile acid patterns found by testing
mass spectrometry showing bile acid changes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe fat-soluble vitamin (A, D, E, K) deficiency
searchTerms: severe deficiency of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera

occasional.symptomName: Coagulopathy due to vitamin K deficiency

blood clotting issues due to vitamin deficiency
coagulopathy linked to vitamin K shortage

occasional.notes: Enlarged spleen secondary to portal hypertension

rare.symptomName: Neurological impairment secondary to vitamin E deficiency
searchTerms: nerve and brain problems from vitamin E lack
neurological symptoms due to vitamin E deficiency

laboratory: Abnormal bile acid profile on mass spectrometry
Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly and possible liver fibrosis
Liver biopsy demonstrating cholestasis and bile duct proliferation
genetic: Pathogenic variants in bile acid synthesis genes such as HSD3B7, AKR1D1, CYP7A1
other: Response to bile acid replacement therapy (e.g., cholic acid) supports diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in ATP8B1, ABCB11 genes
Absence of abnormal bile acid metabolites
Characteristic PAS-positive globules on liver biopsy

redFlags: Severe fat-soluble vitamin deficiency with bleeding diathesis
Failure to thrive despite nutritional support
